clue.text: United cell is ready for insertion into broken toe

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: for insertion into tells us the word for ready goes inside the other piece
broken signals that the letters of toe are rearranged

parts.note: game means willing or ready, as in game for anything

explanation.surface: A biology note about a combined cell being prepared for implanting into an injured toe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' suggests prepared, but here it is the sense 'willing', as in game for anything; 'broken' makes OTE, and 'United' describes the cell's fusing with its twin.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a reproductive cell that fuses with a partner of the same size and form, so it is united.

indicators.note: inside places the general within the word for agent

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
Robert E. Lee, the Confederate general

explanation.surface: A dozing secret agent with a senior officer tucked inside his ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodding off is what a drowsy person does, so nodding describes someone heavy-eyed.

clue.text: Clue for cat arises from what escalates?

definitions.meaning: the second word of this answer, when set in motion, rearranges into the letters of cat arises
a cryptic description of an escalator, which carries people upward

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is itself an anagram clue: the first word is the anagram signal, and the nine letters after it shuffle into CAT ARISES.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalator is a powered flight of steps that rises on its own, a literal description of what escalates.

clue.text: Back seats worth their weight in gold?

parts.note: a tonne is a metric unit of weight
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Rear seats in a car so prized they are worth their weight in gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface idiom 'worth their weight in gold' hides the plain sum: a weight followed by gold.
explanation.definitionFit: On early motor cars this was the rear compartment holding the back passenger seats.

clue.text: Painter left without setter or soldier

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for left wraps round the rest

parts.note: gone means left, departed
the setter refers to himself as I
taken as written
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An artist walked out, leaving behind neither the puzzle-setter nor a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside: G...ONE surrounds I, OR and GI.
explanation.definitionFit: Giorgione was a Venetian painter of the High Renaissance, known for The Tempest.

clue.text: Petty authoritarianism to be doled out in the morning

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are distributed in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
a.m. stands for the morning, before noon

explanation.surface: Small-minded officiousness is handed out every morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges DOLED together with AM, the abbreviation for the morning, into ADLEDOM, set after BE.
explanation.definitionFit: A beadle was a minor parish official, and the word for that class stands for fussy officiousness.

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short at the tail, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a statue is a sculpted representation of a figure
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A legal depiction cut back by a Conservative politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set down by statute is required or permitted by law, hence legal.

clue.text: Pioneering ecological book is back, fast bound

indicators.note: back tells us the little word is turned round

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting
a bound is a leap, a spring

explanation.surface: A trailblazing environmental volume has returned, and is tightly bound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IS into SI. 'fast bound' reads as one phrase, but it is two words: a fast and a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Rachel Carson's 1962 book on pesticides helped launch the modern environmental movement.

clue.text: Accommodation for still needy borrower is clue to 13

definitions.meaning: a loan facility that is renewed as it is repaid, for someone who keeps needing money
this phrase is itself an anagram clue, its first word the signal and its second the letters, giving the first word of 13

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a clue, the first word means turning round and the second word's letters, so turned, spell DIRECT.
explanation.definitionFit: A facility of this kind lets a borrower draw again on the funds once repaid, ideal for a habitual debtor.

clue.text: Adaptable — now may we leave the course?

definitions.text: now may we leave the course?
definitions.meaning: golfers asking whether the Open championship is over so they can go home

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into OPEN ENDED: the Open is the British Open golf championship.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no fixed end can be changed or extended at will, so it is adaptable.

parts.note: to direct a project is to oversee it
a jab is an injection, as from a needle

explanation.surface: A supervisor asks about a vaccine shot, and is told no carburettor is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed' tempts a reading about medical needles, but the definition is engineering.
explanation.definitionFit: In this engine system fuel is sprayed straight into the cylinders, doing away with the carburettor.

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the first piece above the second

parts.note: a star is a light in the sky
board stands for a ship, as in on board

explanation.surface: Is that a navigation light on the right-hand side of a vessel?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a ship's green right-hand lamp, which is neatly in the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the nautical term for the right-hand side of a vessel when facing forward.

clue.text: Prophetic Persian heard in front of Greek

indicators.note: heard tells us the word for Persian is taken by its sound

parts.note: Farsi is the Persian language
taken as written

indicators.note: front of picks out the opening letter of Greek

explanation.surface: A Persian prophet is overheard ahead of a Greek one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in front of' looks like a single positional phrase; here IN is a piece and 'front of' picks the G of Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophetic person sees far into the future, which is just what this compound describes.

parts.note: to place something is to put it
Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals

explanation.surface: Station a veteran soldier on the banks of the River Thames.
explanation.walkthrough: Ney was Napoleon's 'bravest of the brave'. PUTNEY is a district of south-west London beside the River Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a London district lying on the south bank of the river, so it is a place on Thames.

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild; the possessive adds no letter
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A deity tries his hand at running a household room.
explanation.definitionFit: A larder or store room for food is a domestic room in a house.

clue.text: Russian girl with stories of French comedian

parts.note: Jacques Tati, the French comic actor and director of Monsieur Hulot films
ana is a collection of anecdotes or sayings about a person

explanation.surface: A Russian girl telling anecdotes about a French comic.
explanation.walkthrough: The stories of Tati come after his name: an 'ana' is a collection of stories about someone, as in Johnsoniana.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Russian girl's name, borne by the heroine of Pushkin's Eugene Onegin.

indicators.note: they say signals a word that is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a ranker is a private soldier, one serving in the ranks

explanation.surface: Someone claims that malice is a personal matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' looks like an adjective meaning personal, but it is the army rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter lasting resentment is a form of spite or malice.

definitions.meaning: to ... a matter is to begin dealing with it

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer into two words, ENTER ON.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the anatomical term for the alimentary canal, the gut.

clue.text: Arrival of fools, perhaps, with trendy aquatic plant

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
a rush is a marsh or water plant

explanation.surface: A crowd of fools turns up to admire a fashionable water plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying 'fools rush in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden incoming surge is an arrival, and fools are proverbially the ones who rush in.

definitions.meaning: an open drill area for troops, where soldiers do square-bashing
read as a clue, the first word's letters are ... up to give a padre

explanation.walkthrough: As a clue, 'ground' is the anagram signal and PARADE shuffles into A PADRE, an army chaplain.
explanation.definitionFit: A military drill area is a square, the place where troops do square-bashing.

parts.note: in web addresses dot is followed by com
fit means suitable or worthy

explanation.surface: Dot's boyfriend is a decent and charming fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dot' looks like a woman's name, but it is the dot of an internet address.
explanation.definitionFit: A sugar-coated seed or nut is an old-fashioned kind of sweet.

clue.text: Without master, criminal society's company a great disappointment

indicators.note: without tells us the master's letters are removed

parts.note: the Mafia is the criminal organisation
MA is a Master of Arts
S is an abbreviation for society; the possessive adds nothing

explanation.surface: Missing their boss, the crime syndicate's business proves a letdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' removes MA from MAFIA, leaving FIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete failure or debacle is a crushing disappointment.

clue.text: Cultural concerns turn to shot in the arm for the army

indicators.note: turn tells us the word for cultural concerns is reversed

parts.note: the arts are culture's concerns
a tonic is a boost, a shot in the arm

explanation.surface: Arts groups argue the military needs a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses ARTS to STRA.
explanation.definitionFit: This rare adjective means relating to an army, from the Greek word for army.

clue.text: Bacon and eggs etc as clue to RAF basket

definitions.meaning: read as a clue, the first word is the signal and the letters of the second word rearrange to RAF BASKET

explanation.walkthrough: As a clue, the first word means cooked up, a common anagram signal, and the second word's letters give RAF BASKET.
explanation.definitionFit: A plate of fried bacon and eggs is the traditional British morning meal.
